current.text: Stewart was traded to Memphis, where he is the backup center behind Zach Edey.
He wants a bigger role and more three-point attempts.
Zach Edey had a broken foot in June. In mid-September an expert said he might be out for longer.
Experts say Stewart can start or make spot starts while Edey is out. That makes him a good late pick if Edey's absence runs long.
The Memphis frontcourt is crowded with Prosper, Hendricks, Edey and Stewart, and Cameron Boozer will start.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo runs an 11-man rotation with short stints and keeps minutes down. Only Boozer and Coward are expected to top 30 minutes, which caps a backup center's minutes.

durable.text: He has not finished a season healthy in the last three or four years.
Blocks are his standout category. He projects to about 1.6 per game, which is far above the top 250 pool.
Steals are a clear weakness, at about 0.3 per game. That is low even for a big man.
